what: The figures the CDISC pilot's own clinical study report printed for Tables 14-1.01, 14-1.02, 14-2.01, 14-4.01, 14-5.01, 14-5.02 and 14-1.03, transcribed cell by cell. open.csr rebuilds those seven displays as t-populations, t-end-of-study, t-demographics, t-exposure, t-ae-incidence, t-sae-incidence and t-subjects-by-site; qc/reference-report-agreement.R checks that a from-scratch recomputation and the committed rendered HTML both land on every string below.

reference.document: Clinical Study Report, CDISC SDTM/ADaM Pilot Project, protocol CDISCPILOT01, FINAL, 27 June 2006

tables.t-populations: Table 14-1.01, Summary of Populations (Population: All Subjects)
tables.t-end-of-study: Table 14-1.02, Summary of End of Study Data (Population: Intent-to-Treat)
tables.t-demographics: Table 14-2.01, Summary of Demographic and Baseline Characteristics (Population: Intent-to-Treat)
tables.t-exposure: Table 14-4.01, Summary of Planned Exposure to Study Drug, as of End of Study (Population: Safety)
tables.t-ae-incidence: Table 14-5.01, Incidence of Treatment Emergent Adverse Events by Treatment Group (Population: Safety)
tables.t-sae-incidence: Table 14-5.02, Incidence of Treatment Emergent Serious Adverse Events by Treatment Group (Population: Safety)
tables.t-subjects-by-site: Table 14-1.03, Summary of Number of Subjects By Site (Population: All Subjects)

reference.produced_by: SAS programs adsl1.sas and adsl2.sas, run 21:02 Monday, 26 June 2006, per the Source line printed on each table.
reference.analysis_plan: Statistical Analysis Plan section 9.7.1.2: 'The number of subjects randomized, the number of subjects in each analysis dataset, and the disposition of subjects were tabulated by treatment group. Specific reasons for early study discontinuation (protocol completed, lack of efficacy, and adverse event) were compared using a Fisher's exact test.' The display shells are Attachment 13.1.1 Templates 1 and 2.
reference.read_for: Printed figures and analysis definitions only. No data was taken from the report or from any repository other than phuse-org/phuse-scripts (MIT).
reference.transcription: Typed from the report by hand, not computed. Whitespace inside the parentheses is as printed; the comparison collapses it. Because it is typed, this is the one route that cannot be re-derived from anything in the repository, so `--verify-transcription` re-reads the source document and checks it; see `source_document` below.

source_document.not_vendored: The PDF is deliberately NOT vendored into this repository. Pages 154-409 of it — the protocol and the sample CRF — carry 'Copyright (c) 2006 Eli Lilly and Company' and are not ours to redistribute. The two pages this record transcribes, 43 and 44, are result tables authored by the CDISC SDTM/ADaM Pilot Project Team and sit outside that range; they are read, not copied.
source_document.verified: 2026-08-27, by `Rscript qc/reference-report-agreement.R --verify-transcription`, against the document whose SHA-256 is pinned above. Every cell, row label and printed p-value below was re-derived from the PDF text and matched. Extended 2026-09-02 (#61) to Tables 14-2.01 (pages 46-48) and 14-4.01 (page 62), re-verified against the same document by the same command. Extended 2026-09-02 (#62) to Tables 14-5.01 (pages 63-78) and 14-5.02 (page 79). Extended 2026-09-02 (#63) to Table 14-1.03 (page 45).
source_document.verification_found: Two errors in the hand transcription, both introduced when this record was first written and both invisible to the three-route comparison because the specs were written from the same misreading: (1) a p-value of 0.5000 recorded against the Death row, which the report does not print — the report prints a p-value on exactly the three rows the SAP names; (2) the two tables' population labels recorded the wrong way round.
source_document.not_in_ci: This check is not a CI step. It needs the network and a PDF text extractor (poppler's pdftotext), and a build that fails because a third-party download was slow teaches people to ignore it. It is a maintainer command, to be run whenever this record is edited. What CI does run is the three-route comparison, which no longer has anything to compare against if this record is wrong — which is exactly why the record's own provenance is pinned here rather than asserted.

comparison.route_a: A from-scratch recomputation in qc/reference-report-agreement.R that reads the vendored adsl.xpt.gz with {haven} and never loads {opencsr}: subject-level flags for the two disposition tables; means, SDs, medians, extremes, ANOVA and chi-square p-values for the demographics table; dose summaries for the exposure table. SAS rounding throughout.
comparison.route_b: The cell text parsed out of the committed outputs/<slug>/<version>/table.html, which is what the pipeline published.
comparison.route_c: This record: what the 2006 SAS programs printed.
comparison.rule: All three must agree on every cell. Any disagreement is exit status 1.

t-demographics.note: The report prints a p-value beside each block's n row (or beside the first level of a sub-block without one): one-way ANOVA for a continuous measure, Pearson's chi-square for a categorical one. `report_label` is the text the report prints before the cells on that line; `label` is what the rendered display prints, which the published-display route reads.

t-exposure.note: The report lays the two populations out as column groups; the rendered display lays them out as row blocks under one set of treatment columns. `published_from` says which rendered row (by its label and the occurrence of that label in reading order) and which columns supply each of the six report cells, in order.

t-ae-incidence.note: Three cells per line — n (%) [events] per arm — and two p-value columns, Fisher's exact test of placebo against each active arm; a blank p-value is a comparison with no subjects on either side. `report_label` keeps the report's wrapped or truncated text; `label` is the term as the data spells it, which the rendered display prints.

t-ae-incidence.known_differences_note: Four of the 227 printed p-values differ from R's two-sided Fisher exact test at the third decimal, each by one thousandth upward, on tables whose exact p sits just under the rounding boundary (0.2085, 0.0575, 0.0025). The subject counts and denominators agree, and no alternative definition tried — the any-event denominator, doubled one-sided, chi-square, denominators within two of the stated N — reproduces all four. They are recorded here as the 2006 program's figures and held to: the comparison fails if any of them closes or any other cell opens.
